summary.title: Computer Architecture: A Quantitative Approach, 7th Edition
summary.one_liner: A widely used textbook by Hennessy, Patterson and Kozyrakis that teaches computer architecture through quantitative design analysis, covering memory hierarchy, instruction-level, data-level and thread-level parallelism, warehouse-scale systems and domain-specific architectures.
takeaways: Quantitative design principles for evaluating processor and system architecture trade-offs
Memory hierarchy and cache design, plus instruction-level and thread-level parallelism
Coverage of GPU, CPU, domain-specific architectures and systems on chip in the 7th edition
Each chapter includes 'Putting It All Together' sections with real-world examples and common architectural traps
summary.summary: This is the publisher page for the 7th edition of Computer Architecture: A Quantitative Approach by John Hennessy, David Patterson and Christos Kozyrakis, published October/December 2025 by Elsevier. The book is described as a long-standing reference for instructors, students and practitioners of computer design. It is organized into chapters on quantitative design fundamentals, memory hierarchy, instruction-level parallelism, data-level parallelism in vector/SIMD/GPU architectures, thread-level parallelism, warehouse-scale systems and domain-specific architectures, with online appendices covering pipelining, storage, interconnection networks and more. Each chapter follows a consistent structure with crosscutting issues, putting-it-all-together sections and examples of common misunderstandings.
